facts.fact: 葬礼在「我」眼里毫无分量：不知道这是什么教派，与她熟悉的香烟缭绕的天主教堂相反，这座教堂无味、线条干净、毫无戏剧性。
facts.anchor: This church was unscented, all clean lines and nothing dramatic to look at.

facts.fact: 愿收 AIDS 死者的殡仪馆很少，「我」怀疑这里向 Mark 母亲加价；他大概更愿意进 potter's field，但「我」随即发现自己从没问过他。
facts.anchor: I knew that there weren’t a lot of funeral homes that would take someone who’d died of AIDS, and I wondered if this place upcharged her.

facts.fact: Mark 母亲两侧是带着一群群金发孩子的姐姐们（孩子被留在家中，怕死者传染）；Mark 是在姐姐们要他为「让母亲难过的同性恋事」多点同情心时，才不再理她们的。
facts.anchor: She was flanked by his older sisters, who each had a brood of blond children who must have been left at home in case the dead man was contagious.

facts.fact: Mark 父亲没来葬礼；此人战时是商船炮手，据称曾在地中海救生筏上熬过四天；Mark 一直想问他那四天在想什么。
facts.anchor: had, allegedly, survived on a life raft for four days on the Mediterranean before being rescued

facts.fact: Mark 评价父亲：硬汉、毫无想象力，认为一切都是必然的。
facts.anchor: “Yeah, but he could never think of life happening differently. Like, he couldn’t even imagine there not being a war, even though he knows more than me how bad it was. Everything was inevitable to him.

facts.fact: Patrick 在教堂后排自设吊唁受宾线，丝绸衬衫解到最后一颗扣；「我」质问他为何不打电话，他只说来不及，最后是 Darryl 把她送上火车。
facts.anchor: Patrick operated his own receiving line in the back of the church

facts.fact: 回程火车与家门口她半路等 Mark 显形而不得；门口的「轮廓」最终认出是自己的渴望在填补空位。
facts.anchor: my own want, filling up the empty space.
